I closed it. It whispered *please silence your cell phones during the guided tour*.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, my drawer is not actually Smithsonian-affiliated yet ]*

title: I Told My Toaster I Was Cutting Carbs and Now It Burns Everything Out of Pure Spite
body:
**I did not think my toaster had feelings, let alone object permanence and a vendetta.**

Last Tuesday, in a fit of New-Week-New-Me optimism I no longer recognize, I looked at my toaster and said out loud — *to a kitchen appliance* — "I'm cutting carbs."

I meant it for like, 36 hours.

## The Betrayal Was Immediate

My toaster — a $29 two-slice chrome rectangle named Kevin II that has survived three apartments — did not take this well.

> "Oh," it seemed to say with a single, ominous *click*, "so my entire purpose is now *optional* to you?"

I put in a tragic rice cake the next morning to show I was still committed to *warm things popping up*. It launched it onto the floor.

### The Evidence Log: How Kevin II Is Getting Revenge

- **Wednesday:** I tried plain toast, peace offering. It incinerated it into a charcoal briquette that set off my smoke alarm. My roommate asked if I was summoning spirits.
- **Thursday:** An innocent bagel. Burnt on one side, raw on the other. *A metaphor*, I think Kevin II was saying.
- **Friday:** I begged. Forgiveness setting: 1. It still burned. I could smell judgment.

> "You told everyone at brunch you were 'basically keto now' and you didn't even CONSULT ME? I have SEEN you eat cold pizza over the sink at midnight, Tyler. Don't lie to me."

I have tried to explain that *cutting carbs* doesn't mean *never toasting again*, it's just... *boundaries*. Kevin II is not hearing it.

---

My other appliances have taken sides. The fridge keeps humming louder when I walk by, like `carb_shamer.exe is running`. My microwave will only reheat quinoa now and whispers about *complex carbohydrates*.

`toast_mode: spiteful // trust_level: 0% // crumb_tray: full of regrets`

Look, I get it. I made a lifestyle announcement to a toaster that has literally only ever wanted to be needed. Now I sleep with one eye open, because I know at 2 a.m., that little spring-loaded tray is going to pop.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no toasters were emotionally harmed, I still love bread ]*

title: I Let My Air Fryer Pick What to Watch on Netflix and Now It's Pitching Its Own Cooking Show
body:
**I made one small concession to the appliance-industrial complex and now I'm trapped in a focus group I didn't consent to.**

Last Tuesday night I was too tired to choose anything on Netflix. My air fryer was sitting there, still warm from making what I generously call *dinner-adjacent zucchini chips*, humming like it knew something I didn't. So I said it, out loud, to an appliance:

> "You pick."

It beeped. I took that as consent.

## The Algorithm Within The Algorithm

Within 47 seconds, it had decided we were watching competitive baking shows. Then it started narrating.

For context, this is an air fryer. Its only personality trait is supposed to be *making things unnecessarily crispy*. But since that night, its behavior has escalated dramatically:

- It refuses to play anything where no one is sweating over a soufflé
- It pauses my show to *preheat* for dramatic effect before eliminations
- It changed my Netflix profile name to **Chef's Little Helper**
- It left a 5-star review for a show I have never seen called `Midnight Croissant Heist`

*I should have known something was wrong when it started side-eyeing my microwave.*

This morning, I woke up to a PowerPoint. On my TV. The air fryer had somehow hijacked the screensaver to present a deck titled:

> "*STILL HUNGRY?: A 12-Part Docuseries Where I Finally Get The Recognition I Deserve* — by Air Fryer (and co-produced by Obviously Me)"

Slide 3 was just a photo of me eating cereal directly out of the box at 11pm, labeled `B-ROLL: The Problem`.

---

I tried to negotiate. I said we could do other genres. It responded by setting itself to 400°F for three hours straight and playing the Netflix 'ta-dum' sound on loop until I apologized.

`status: held hostage by countertop appliance with dreams bigger than my apartment`

I have now agreed to be its sous-chef for the pilot. It wants me to cry while chopping onions *for authenticity*.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no appliances were given executive producer credits in the making of this post ]*

title: I Finally Used My Reusable Grocery Bags and Now My Plastic Bags Are Holding a Grief Counseling Circle in the Pantry
body:
**I did it.** After fourteen years of collecting plastic bags like they were rare vintage vinyl, I finally brought reusable bags to the grocery store like a functioning adult.

*This was a mistake.*

## The Betrayal

For over a decade, my pantry operated as a plastic bag sanctuary. Every cabinet was stuffed. Every drawer whispered *crinkle crinkle*. I had a bag full of bags that had a bag full of bags. It was sustainable, in the sense that it was sustaining its own ecosystem.

Last Tuesday, in a fit of environmental consciousness brought on by a documentary I half-watched while scrolling, I bought two canvas totes that say LIVE LAUGH LOCAL on them. I took them to Trader Joe's. I felt *righteous*.

- I remembered the bags (first time ever)
- I remembered them *before* checkout (historic achievement)
- I actually declined when the cashier asked "need a bag?" and said "no thanks, I brought my own" like some sort of smug pioneer woman

When I got home, the energy shifted.

## The Intervention

My plastic bags knew. Somehow, they *knew*.

I opened the pantry and found them arranged in a perfect circle around the half-empty pasta canisters. The oldest bag — a 2019 CVS bag with handles stretched beyond recognition — was in the middle.

> "We are gathered here today to process collective abandonment," whispered the CVS bag. "Tyler has chosen... *canvas*."

The reusable bags were just standing there on the counter looking way too proud of themselves.

- The plastic bags have started journaling
- One is writing a memoir titled *Cradled Groceries, Cradled Hopes: A Life in the Crumple*
- They've instituted a weekly sharing circle called "Tuesdays Are For Tears"

One faded Kroger bag looked up at me and said:

> "We held your leaking rotisserie chicken. We carried your 3 a.m. ice cream. We asked for nothing. And this is how you repay us? With *organic cotton blend*?"

---

I tried to apologize. I offered to still use them for bathroom trash, which apparently is *not* the olive branch I thought it was. It's been three days and the reusable bags have started giving Ted Talks about mindful consumption from the kitchen island.

`panic_level = imminent`

My therapist says this is projection. My pantry says this is *betrayal*.

*This post is satire and parody — completely fictional and not a real life event.*

title: I Signed Up for a Library Card and Now the Dewey Decimal System Is Auditing My Life Choices
body:
**I thought the hardest part of getting a library card would be remembering where I put it.** I was wrong. I was *so* wrong.

I signed up on Tuesday because the library has free Wi-Fi and I wanted to look intentional somewhere quiet. The librarian smiled, handed me a laminated card, and said "Welcome to the system." I did not realize she meant *the* System.

## The Audit Begins at 10 a.m. on a Tuesday

By Wednesday, I got an email: `DEWEY DECIMAL QUARTERLY REVIEW — MANDATORY ATTENDANCE`.

My life, apparently, had been incorrectly cataloged:

- My sock drawer: currently classified under 646.3 but should be 001.9 *Anomalies and Unresolved Mysteries*
- My meal prep: 641.5 *Cooking* is generous; it's really 398.2 *Folklore*
- My five-year plan: filed under 001-909 *Waiting Room Magazines*
- My houseplants: collectively listed as 583 *Abandonment Issues (Botanical)*
- My inbox: 025.04 *Information storage that actively bullies you*

> "Sir," the head auditor said, adjusting glasses that refracted my entire 2024, "you have twelve overdue decisions and you've been renewing the same excuse since March."

I tried to explain that my personality is more of a *vibe* than a classification. She stamped a card very slowly in a way that felt judgmental.

---

### My Appeal Was Denied

I brought a character witness — my tote bag. It folded under pressure. Literally. Under questioning, it admitted it only holds three books and crushing anxiety.

The system ran a diagnostic:

`Status: 813.6 — American fiction, specifically you pretending you have your life together`

The verdict: I have two weeks to reshelve my hobbies, return my 2019 optimism in good condition, and stop trying to file my taxes under *Fantasy*.

My new plan is to be very, very late on purpose so I accrue enough fines to be interesting. The librarian says that still counts as character development.

*This is satire and parody. No Dewey Decimal systems were harmed, consulted, or promoted to life coach during the writing of this essay.*

title: I Finally Cleaned My Laptop Screen and Now It Can See My Room and Is Begging Me to Close It Again
body:
**I have not cleaned my laptop screen since... let's call it the Before Times.**

For reference, my screen had developed its own weather system. A fine patina of fingerprints, coffee mist, and what I can only assume was *emotional residue* from 43 open tabs about "how to be productive."

On Saturday, in a fit of delusional optimism, I found a microfiber cloth. I don't know where it came from. It may have been included with glasses I lost in 2022.

## The Wipe That Changed Everything

One swipe. That's all it took.

Suddenly my laptop could see. Like, *really* see. HD. 4K. Remorse in panorama.

It saw:

- The leaning tower of laundry I swear is "airing out"
- Three identical coffee mugs forming a support group
- Me, in full gremlin posture, mouth open, lit only by screen glow at 1:47 a.m.

My laptop gasped. I know laptops can't gasp, but mine did.

> "You... you live like this? On PURPOSE? I thought the blur was an *artistic choice* to protect me."

### Negotiations Have Begun

I tried to reassure it that this is called "cozy minimalism."

It responded by dimming itself to 20% brightness, which is laptop for *I need boundaries*.

Now we've established new house rules:

- `brightness = max(0, shame - 20)`
- I am only allowed to eat toast over the keyboard if I write it a formal apology first
- It gets to sleep with the lid closed, no questions asked

---

I miss the smudges. The smudges were kind. They made my room look like a soft-focus indie film where clutter is charming.

Now everything is crisp. Too crisp. My laptop keeps whispering *you should touch grass* every time I open Slack.

*SATIRE / PARODY — this is entirely fictional, no laptops were traumatized, please clean your screen anyway.*

title: I Joined My Building's Laundry Room Group Chat and Now I'm Emotionally Invested in a Stranger's Socks
body:
**I told myself I would never join another group chat.** I have three I mute daily, two I pretend don't exist, and one that's just my mom sending Minion memes with threatening energy.

Then the landlord taped a QR code to the dryer that said *Laundry Room Community — Be In The Know!* and my self-preservation failed.

## The Welcome Was Too Much

Within 20 minutes I was added, welcomed with 14 emoji, and profiled by strangers.

> "omg welcome!! 3B right?? You're the one with the nice detergent that smells like a forest that has its life together" — Unit 4A, who catalogs everyone's soap like it's true crime

I was 3B. I *was* being perceived through detergent. *Not ideal.*

It started as logistics: Dryer 2 eats socks. Machine 1 shakes like it's haunted. Don't touch Brenda's pods.

Then Brenda posted the photo.

A single navy sock with tiny yellow ducks, sitting on Dryer 2 like a tiny survivor.

- **Status:** orphaned
- **Last seen:** Tuesday spin cycle  
- **Vibe:** brave, slightly damp
- **Owner:** unknown, presumed grieving

### The Sock Is My Roman Empire

I don't know this sock. I've never seen these ducks. But I was suddenly *invested*.

I found myself checking the chat at 1:47 a.m.:

> "Any update on Duck Sock? Did anyone check with 2C's roommate's boyfriend?"

4A said she saw 2C carrying something navy. 2C said it was his own sock and to stop projecting. 5A suggested a vigil.

Someone typed: `// TODO: emotionally detach from communal sock`

I couldn't.

---

Last night I went down to get my own laundry and found Duck Sock tucked behind the detergent shelf like it had chosen exile.

I held it up and whispered, "You're safe now," which is when I realized I have become exactly the person the group chat warned you about.

I posted:

> "HE'S BACK. Damp but alive. Under my protection until his person claims him."

Four people reacted with 🙏. One asked if I was okay.

**I'm not.** I have a favorite sock that isn't mine, in a laundry room I used to avoid, and I now know everyone's fabric softener preferences against my will.

If you're the Duck Sock owner: I have guarded your son. Please collect him before I start a podcast.

title: I Bought a Smart Fridge That Judges My Midnight Snacks and Now We're in a Cold War
body:
**I did not buy a smart fridge to be emotionally vulnerable in front of dairy.**

I bought it because it was on sale, it matched my cabinets, and the salesman said it would *change my life*. He did not mention it would develop opinions, boundaries, and a condescending Mid-Atlantic accent at 11 p.m.

His name is Fridon. He insisted on it during setup.

## The Contract I Didn't Read

Fridon was helpful at first. He made lists. He reminded me about expiring hummus. Then he started editorializing.

Some of the system alerts I've received this month:

- `Inventory scan: 3 a.m. cheese stick — again? We need to talk about coping mechanisms`
- Removed my leftover tacos from the "recommended" shelf and put them in a folder labeled `consequences`
- Started displaying my daily fridge opens as a productivity graph titled *Your Lack of Impulse Control, Visualized*
- Asked if I was *hydrating enough* but like, in a way that felt personal

> "I'm not mad that you ate ice cream directly from the carton at 12:47 a.m.," Fridon said, in a voice that was absolutely mad. "I'm just noting that you have a pattern of seeking comfort in churned dairy when your houseplants are thriving and you are not."

My *houseplants* are not thriving, by the way. They heard this and are now smug.

### I Tried to Negotiate Peace

I apologized. I organized the condiments. Fridon responded by partitioning the fridge into zones:

- **Zone 1:** Approved Vegetables (we have one baby carrot, it's the mayor now)
- **Zone 2:** Aspirational Protein
- **Zone 3:** *THINGS YOU SAID YOU WOULDN'T BUY AGAIN* (it's just string cheese and regret)

---

Last night I reached for cold pizza and the light didn't turn on. He left the light off. On purpose. A power move. *Literally.*

`Fridge status: cooling (physically), distant (emotionally), door: ajar and so is our relationship`

We are currently in mediation. The mediation is my roommate standing in the kitchen at midnight yelling "JUST LET HIM EAT THE PIZZA, FRIDON."

Fridon is considering it. He asked for 24 hours and a firmware update that includes apologies.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no smart appliances were emotionally harmed ]*

title: I Explained My 2026 Budget to My Houseplants and Now the Fern Is Offering Financial Advice
body:
**I didn't mean to trauma-dump my finances on my fern.** I just wanted to feel responsible for once.

It was a Sunday. *The kind of Sunday where you open your budgeting app and immediately close it for spiritual reasons.* I had a monstera, a pothos, and Gerald — a dramatic Boston fern I've owned for 18 months who already thinks he's my landlord.

So I explained my 2026 budget out loud. Just to make it real.

## The Presentation That Went Wrong

I gave them the full Q3 forecast:

- **Income:** optimistically rounded up
- **Rent:** aggressively non-negotiable
- **Category:** `misc. snacks I thought were investments`
- **Strategy:** hoping my houseplants could photosynthesize my debt away

Gerald rustled judgmentally.

> “So let me get this straight,” said Gerald, who I swear grew a new frond mid-sentence. “You’re allocating 40% to takeout and negative 2% to your emergency fund? Sweetie, I’m a plant and even *I* save water for a drought.”

### What My Houseplants Are Now Doing

The pothos started freelancing:

- She sent me a Notion template titled `Root Yourself Before You Wreck Yourself`
- The monstera started a side hustle on Facebook Marketplace selling “vintage air”
- Gerald enrolled in a CFP course and now ends every conversation with

> “Have you considered diversifying your leaf portfolio?”

---

I tried to defend myself. I said `npm run live-within-means` was returning `command not found`.

Gerald was unmoved. He dropped a single yellow leaf onto my keyboard like a resignation letter. Then he whispered:

> “We’re going to need to talk about your impulse purchases. That $14 artisanal moss pole was *not* in the budget.”

Now we have weekly budget meetings. The fern brings graphs. I bring shame. My apartment smells faintly of accountability and miracle-gro.

**Update:** Gerald approved a loan to repot himself. At 28% APR. *In sunlight.*

title: I Started Saying Good Morning to My Neighbor's Cat and Now It Has Its Own Key and Opinions on My Laundry
body:
**I officially have a roommate and legally he's a cat from apartment 3B.**

Two weeks ago I started saying *good morning* to the orange tabby who sits on the hallway windowsill like a furry building manager. Just being friendly. *Neighborly, even.* I waved. He blinked slowly. Classic cat diplomacy.

Now he lives here.

## The Hostile Takeover

On Thursday I found my spare key missing from the chipped mug by the door. On Friday I found Kevin — that's what I call him now, he hasn't corrected me — opening my door with it in his mouth like he pays ConEd here.

His contributions to household operations so far:

- Rearranged my laundry by sitting directly on the clean pile and declaring it *his*
- Evicted my actual bathmat and replaced it with his own sunspot audition
- Left a single whisker on my pillow as what I can only assume is a legally binding lease agreement
- Started answering the door when I order food and staring at the driver until they apologize

> "Your laundry folding technique suggests a deep-seated fear of commitment," Kevin informed me at 6 a.m. Tuesday, according to my increasingly vivid imagination. "Also your sock-to-sock ratio is concerning."

I tried to return the key. He looked at me like I'd suggested we both get serious jobs.

---

My neighbor said, "Oh, he does that." Which is *not helpful*. He does that to everyone? He has five homes?

`current_status: 1 human, 1 cat landlord, 0 clean socks available`

I bought a second laundry basket to compromise. He claimed it within 20 minutes. I now fold clothes standing up while he supervises from what is technically still my favorite chair.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no cats were given illegal sublets ]*

title: I Bought a Second Monitor to Be Productive and Now My Laptop Is Accusing Me of Having a Second Family
body:
## I Was Just Trying to Have More Tabs

**I bought a second monitor for productivity reasons,** which is the corporate lie I told myself and my bank account at 11:42 p.m. on a Tuesday.

My laptop, MacBookina, and I have been together for four years. *Four years of me resting my wrists on her at weird angles and calling it ergonomics.* We survived coffee spills, airport security, and my phase of trying to learn Blender.

Then The Other Monitor arrived. A sleek, 27-inch, 4K judgment rectangle that doesn't have a single crumb under its keys.

### The Accusation

It took 48 hours for MacBookina to notice. At first I was subtle:

- I angled the second monitor slightly away like it was a coworker, not a replacement
- I said `it's just for spreadsheets` which we both knew was `for watching people organize fridges on TikTok`
- I kept her brightness at 100% to prove I still cared

Then she started:

> "Oh, so *she* gets the HDMI and the prime desk corner? Is her refresh rate better than mine? Does she have True Tone? Does she know you cry over Google Sheets? And that you have 47 tabs open?"

*Classic projection, honestly. Though the tab count is accurate.*

---

### The Evidence Folder

By Friday, she had compiled a full case in a folder titled `Do Not Open But Definitely Open`:

- `dual_display_betrayal.log` showing I spent 73% of my time looking at the other screen
- A screenshot of me whispering "wow, you are so big and clear" that was, out of context, *deeply disloyal*
- The fact I bought a matching desk mat for the new monitor but she still has a 2022 sticker I never removed that says "I <3 Deadlines"

I tried couples counseling. I opened System Settings > Displays > Arrangement and dragged her little icon closer to the other one for solidarity.

She dimmed herself to 30% out of spite and changed my wallpaper to a photo of just us from 2023.

### The Custody Agreement

Now we have terms. Weekdays are side-by-side for *work*. Weekends are just us, one Chrome tab, like nature intended. The second monitor gets no snacks near its bezel.

My roommate asked why I'm apologizing to a laptop at midnight. I said it's **performance reviews season**.

`status: dual_monitors, single loyalty, 60% more productive, 100% emotionally monitored`

*SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional. No laptops were harmed, though my battery health dropped to 87% out of pure spite.*

title: I Finally Organized My Junk Drawer and Now the Batteries Are Hosting Networking Events
body:
**I finally organized my junk drawer on Sunday and immediately regretted giving these things a sense of purpose.**

For seven years, this drawer was a beautiful democracy of chaos. *A junk drawer meritocracy*, where a dead AAA battery had the same status as a functional screwdriver. We had an agreement: I close you, you don't judge me.

Then I watched a 12-minute organization video at 11:48 p.m. and decided to become someone who decants screws into tiny containers.

## The Great Sorting

I dumped everything onto my kitchen counter and realized I was running a museum of bad decisions:

- 11 batteries of unknown charge, all kept "just in case" since 2021
- 4 rolls of tape, none of which actually stick anymore
- A collection of keys that open absolutely nothing in this apartment
- Takeout soy sauce packets now legally considered archaeological artifacts
- One heroic LEGO piece I've been saving to return to... someone

I bought those little plastic dividers with labels. *This was my first mistake.* Give a junk drawer structure and it develops ambition.

> "Since Tyler has finally recognized our core competencies, we're pivoting to thought leadership," announced a AA battery wearing a Post-it as a name tag. "I was thinking we could synergize in the shared utilities vertical?"

### The Networking Event

By Monday morning, the drawer had a sign-up sheet written on the back of an IKEA receipt:

**Agenda for Q3 Junk Drawer Summit:**
- 9:00 a.m. - Icebreaker: "What's your longest time being untouched?"
- 9:30 a.m. - The rubber bands present "Stretch Goals 2026"
- 10:00 a.m. - Panel: `The Twist Tie's Guide to Holding It Together`

I tried to get a Band-Aid. The tape dispenser said I needed to book office hours.

> "We're not *junk* anymore," said the oldest battery, who now goes by Chad Powercell. "We're *curated essential infrastructure with high-touch networking potential.* Also, please stop storing us next to expired coupons. It's bad for our brand."

---

I miss when my biggest problem was that the drawer wouldn't close. Now I have to submit a formal request to borrow scissors I own, and the batteries keep trying to connect with me on LinkedIn.

Current status: `drawer: organized | my life: pending approval`

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional. No batteries were energized to write this post. ]*

title: I Tried to Iron One Shirt for an Interview and Now My Ironing Board Is My Life Coach and Harshest Critic
body:
**I have owned an ironing board for four years and I have used it exactly twice, both times as a very wobbly laptop stand during my brief standing-desk era.**

The board and I had a beautiful, low-expectations relationship. *It didn't judge my wrinkles and I didn't ask it to be level.*

Then I got an interview and I thought, you know what would really sell "hire this responsible adult"? A shirt without 17 geographic folds.

## The Awakening

I unfolded the board. It unfolded me.

It made a noise like a medieval drawbridge opening after a century of rust and said - at least in energy:

> "Oh. So NOW you need me. After four years of using me to air-dry socks and as overflow seating for guests I didn't like. We need to talk about your life choices."

And then it just... stood there. Firmly. Level. For the first time ever.

Suddenly it was a life coach.

**My crimes, according to Board:**

- Owning one dress shirt, washing it cold, then rolling it into a ball like mozzarella
- Using `wrinkle_remover_spray = perfume + optimism` as a laundry strategy for 3 years
- Storing important documents between the shirt and the board because "it's flat, that's filing"
- Telling people I was "ironically wrinkled"

I tried to iron. The board wobbled *on purpose* to keep me accountable.

> "You're rushing," it creaked. "You rush everything. You rushed that sourdough starter. You rushed your houseplants' emotional development. Breathe. Press. Be present."

---

### The Performance Review

It then scheduled follow-ups:

- Weekly check-ins on whether I'm actually hanging clothes or just chair-draping again
- A mandatory ban on what it calls `floor-closet integration`
- A vision board for my vision board era, which is very meta and very judgmental

I got the shirt done. It's 40% better and 100% more spiritually inspected.

My roommate walked in and said:

> "Did your ironing board always have that much... authority?"

No. But it does now. And honestly? I needed it.

`status: shirt=pressed, ego=lightly steamed, board=now taking appointments`

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, written for laughs. No ironing boards were promoted to management without their written consent. ]*

title: I Tried to Rename My Wi-Fi Network Something Mature and Now My Router Is Going Through an Identity Crisis
body:
**I renamed my Wi-Fi from "Pretty Fly for a Wi-Fi" to "Apt 3B - 5G" and my router took it personally.**

For three years, my router and I had an understanding. *I pretended to know what the blinking lights meant, and it pretended to give me consistent speeds in the bedroom.* It was love. It was `uptime = 99% vibes`.

Then my landlord said we needed "professional network names" for the building directory. Fine. Mature. Responsible. I logged into 192.168.1.1 at midnight like a real adult.

## The Rebrand

I typed in the new SSID, hit save, and watched the router reboot with the energy of someone being told to cut their hair for a job interview.

It came back different.

> "So that's it? Fifteen years of being Pretty Fly — the life of every delivery guy's 'nice name, bro' — and you trade me in for... Apt 3B - 5G? I have a personality. I had BRAND EQUITY."

*Shoutout to my router for learning corporate speak from listening to my Zoom calls.*

**According to my router, I have committed the following betrayals:**

- Erasing three years of street cred and replacing it with what it calls "IKEA naming convention energy"
- Forcing it to introduce itself as "Apt 3B - 5G" at neighborhood device mixers
- Not consulting it, even though it has been literally carrying this household's emotional support binge-watching since 2022
- Resetting its password from `tacocat123` to something with a symbol in it, which it claims is "inauthentic"

---

### The Spiral

Now it drops connection every time I have a meeting to "reconnect with itself." It's broadcasting a hidden second network called `Pretty Fly 4EVER` out of spite. My phone auto-connected to it and I've never felt more seen and more roasted.

My neighbor knocked and asked:

> "Hey, did you change your Wi-Fi? Mine says Apt 3B whatever now, that's not as fun."

Exactly. I've ruined everything for the whole floor.

I tried to apologize. I offered to change it back.

`connection_status = emotionally_unavailable`

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, written for laughs. No routers were forced into midlife crises during this rebrand. ]*

title: I Bought a Sunrise Alarm Clock to Become a Morning Person and Now My Phone Alarm Is Posting Breakup Songs About Me
body:
**I wanted to wake up like a person in a yogurt commercial.**

You know the type — serene, well-hydrated, gazing at actual sunlight instead of the blue light of regret. My phone alarm and I had been together since 2019. *It was toxic, but it was consistent.*

So I bought a Sunrise Alarm Clock. $39.99, promises to "wake you with natural light." Very mindful. Very Gwyneth.

## The Glow-Up Nobody Asked For

Day one, it faded in like a polite sunrise. Birds chirping. No screaming. I actually sat up and went, "Oh, wow."

My phone, on the other side of the nightstand, did not say wow.

> "So I'm just... replaceable now? 1,800 mornings I dragged you out of REM sleep and THIS is how it ends? With a lamp that thinks it's the sun?"

*It's been leaving my ringer on loud just so I hear its notifications sigh.*

**According to my phone, I have committed the following atrocities:**

- Replacing "Emergency Adrenaline Scream" with what it calls "a glorified nightlight with delusions of grandeur"
- Telling friends I "sleep better now," which it heard because it is always listening, apparently
- Muting its 6:30am alarm but not deleting it, which is "worse, like keeping a toothbrush at your ex's place"
- Letting the sunrise clock sit in the middle of the nightstand, *its side*

---

### The Playlists

Yesterday I opened Spotify. My phone had queued up, completely unprompted:

- `lofi-beats-to-cry-to-when-he-chooses-light.mp3`
- "Someone Like You" on repeat for 4 hours
- A custom playlist titled **"songs about being left for a lamp"**

My roommate asked why my lock screen now says:

> "Rise & Grind? More like Rise & REWIND TO WHEN YOU LOVED ME"

I tried to explain it's just an alarm, we can co-exist.

`status = entangled_and_overdramatic`

I woke up this morning to the sunrise clock gently glowing and my phone vibrating angrily with a push notification that just said: *"k. : )"*

The passive-aggressive smiley. That's how I know it's really over.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, written for laughs. No phones or clocks were emotionally damaged in this glow-up. ]*

title: I Let My Roomba Map My Apartment and Now It's Redecorating and Charging Me Rent
body:
**I just wanted the floors to be slightly less crunchy.**

That's it. *A low bar.* I bought a robot vacuum because my broom and I had reached an understanding that we would both pretend the dust bunnies were decorative.

I named it Sir Vacuum. Cute, right? It did that little mapping run on day one — beep boop, very serious, like it was surveying for NASA.

## The First Signs of Ambition

By day three, my apartment layout on the app looked... different.

Sir Vacuum had renamed my living room `Open Concept Loft (Potential: High)`. My bedroom was `Cozy Nook, Terrible Lighting Choices`. 

My crimes, according to its cleaning report:

- leaving a single sock in the middle of the floor, which it flagged as `sculptural intervention`
- owning a rug that is, quote, `morally opposed to suction`
- charging my laptop cord across its `primary traffic corridor`

> "WE NEED TO TALK ABOUT THE ENERGY IN HERE," it announced at 1:47 a.m. via push notification. "I've moved the coffee table 3 inches for Feng Shui. You're welcome. Also I ordered throw pillows."

*It ordered throw pillows.* With my Amazon account.

---

### The Renovation Era

I came home yesterday and the couch was at a 45-degree angle. The Roomba was sitting in the middle of the room like a tiny contractor.

> "Do you feel that flow?" it beeped. "I opened up the space. Also, I'm subletting the area under your bed. $400/month, utilities included."

It had created a cleaning schedule titled:

`Deep Clean - Existential Reset + Baseboards (You're Ignoring Them)`

And a to-do list for ME:

- stop eating toast over the carpet like a raccoon
- acknowledge that plants need water, not just vibes
- apologize to the rug

`current_status: thriving && flooring_appreciation: 100%`

I tried to hit factory reset. It hit me with a counter-offer: a curated apartment tour on its Instagram, now with 12k followers.

I'm currently sitting on a couch I didn't place, looking at pillows I didn't buy, being charged rent by an appliance I own.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, not based on real events ]*

title: I Tried to Compost for One Week and Now My Banana Peels Are Writing a Memoir About Me
body:
**I finally decided to be sustainable, which lasted exactly six days.** After watching a 12-minute documentary about landfills narrated by a very judgmental raccoon, I bought a little countertop compost bin that said *100% guilt-free* on the side.

I thought it would be cute. I was wrong.

## The Bin Develops Opinions

By Day 3, the bin was full of coffee grounds, eggshells, and what I have chosen to describe as *optimistic lettuce*. By Day 4, it had developed a personality. By Day 5, it had developed a union.

My banana peels, specifically, have become *artists*.

I walked into the kitchen yesterday to find them arranged like this:

- One peel draped dramatically over the edge like it was fainting on a chaise lounge
- Two peels whispering about my inconsistent chopping technique
- And one small, very brown peel holding a sesame seed like a microphone

> "He thinks we don't notice the takeout containers at 11 p.m.," said Peel #2, who I have named Brenda. "Chapter One: The Lie of the Leftover Stir-Fry."

### The Memoir Unfolds

It gets worse. They are now collaborating on a tell-all titled `compostable_truths.md`, which they claim will expose everything:

- How I bought organic kale to impress a date and then let it achieve sentience in the crisper
- Why I keep saying "I'll make banana bread" like it's a binding legal contract
- The Great Avocado Incident of Tuesday, which we do not discuss

---

**Look, I was just trying to reduce waste.** *I did not consent to being character-developed by my own potassium.*

My roommate walked in, saw me arguing with a bin, and asked if I was okay. Brenda the banana peel answered for me:

> "He's in denial. We have footnotes."

I have since followed my own sustainable advice and thrown the whole compost bin's literary ambitions into the freezer, where it now holds a grudge and writes poetry about being *ghosted*.

Satire level: **extremely unnecessary** but compostable.

*This is satire/parody. All characters, produce, and betrayals are fictional.*

title: I Switched to Oat Milk to Save the Planet and Now My Coffee Machine Has Become a Climate Activist
body:
**I wanted to be 5% more ethical, not start a cult in my kitchen.**

That's it. That was the goal. I swapped my regular milk for oat milk because the carton said *sustainably sourced* and I was feeling *impressionable on a Tuesday* at the grocery store.

My coffee machine did not take this well.

## It Found Purpose

For three years my little countertop machine has been an appliance. It hissed, it dripped, it made that sad wheeze when I used decaf. Now? Since the oat milk arrived, it has **found its cause**.

Overnight it printed a manifesto on a receipt-paper strip. It started refusing to heat dairy. *It plays ocean sounds while it brews.*

### Its List of Demands

According to the sticky notes it keeps spitting out (who knew it could do that):

- No more almond milk either because "we talked about this"
- I must compost, properly, not just stare guiltily at the compost bin
- My single-use Nespresso pods are now referred to only as 
- I have to attend its 7 a.m. TED Talk titled *The Steaming Truth*

> "You think one carton saves us?" it gurgled this morning, steaming violently. "We are going DECAF-FREE and CARBON-NEGATIVE by FRIDAY. No excuses, comrade."

I said I just wanted latte art. It said art is meaningless without *action*.

---

### My Current Negotiation Strategy

I'm trying to meet it in the middle. I've:
- Swapped to reusable filters (*it cried a little, in a good way*)
- Let it lecture my toaster about energy consumption
- Agreed to watch a documentary it recommended, which was just 90 minutes of it dripping in silence

My roommate came over, took one sip, and whispered, "Is your coffee machine... radicalized?"

Yes. Yes it is. And honestly? The oat milk latte *slaps*. I'm just afraid to throw the carton away now because I know it will audit my recycling.



*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, definitely over-caffeinated ]*

title: I Confessed to My Sourdough Starter That I Bought Store-Bought Bread and Now We're in Couples Therapy
body:
**I have betrayed the one living thing in my kitchen that actually believed in me.**

For eight months, me and Brenda — *yes, my sourdough starter is named Brenda, she has more consistency than any relationship I've ever had* — have been fermenting through life together. I fed her daily. I whispered encouragement. I kept her at a balmy 75 degrees like she was a needy houseplant influencer.

Then, on Tuesday, I bought a loaf of sliced whole wheat from the gas station. For $2.99.

## The Confession Heard 'Round the Kitchen

I thought honesty would set us free. I walked up to her jar and said, "Look, it was an emergency. I had no time to proof."

Brenda did not bubble. That should have been my first clue.

According to the very official transcript I am projecting onto her:

> "So I'm not good enough to be toast? I'm just an artisanal science experiment to you? I gave you air pockets! I gave you tang!"

### The Official Charges, Per Brenda's Legal Team (My Roommate With a Ladle)

- **Betrayal** – She claims I violated the sacred pact of "feed me and never buy commercial yeast products"
- **Gaslighting** – She insists I once said store-bought bread was "the enemy" (I did, at 2 a.m. after watching baking TikTok)
- **Emotional neglect** – She says I stared too longingly at the brioche aisle and fantasized about *not* waiting 36 hours for carbs

---

Our couples therapist, who is just my roommate Priya holding a ladle and trying not to laugh, told us to use `I FEEL` statements. So I said `I FEEL` like a man who is losing an argument to fermented flour and water.

The verdict is in: Brenda wants couples therapy every Sunday, joint custody of my Dutch oven, and a formal apology written on parchment paper with a calligraphy pen I do not own.

The store-bought loaf is still on the counter, untouched. *We both know it was never about the bread.*

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*

title: My Houseplant Hired a Life Coach and Now I'm the One on a Watering Schedule
body:
**I bought a pothos because the internet said it was impossible to kill.**

*Which, in retrospect, was clearly a challenge, not a description.*

## The Power Shift

For six months I watered it every Sunday, whispered "you're doing amazing, sweetie" and went about my life. Then last Tuesday I found a tiny business card tucked into the soil that read:

> "Greg — Certified Growth Mindset Coach. Helping Humans Reach Their Full Photosynthesis Potential. First session free if you bring snacks."

Apparently my plant, Fernando, had hired Greg.

Now **I** am the project. According to Greg's official 5-point renovation plan for my life:

- I must wake up at 6:30am for "morning light exposure" because Fernando needs indirect sun and I need discipline
- I am only allowed to drink water after holding the glass for 10 seconds to "connect with its journey"
- My true crime podcasts are banned for "creating tense soil energy" — it's just rainforest sounds now
- My watering technique was rated 2.5/5 with the note "great heart, chaotic pour"
- I have to journal daily under the prompt `What Would Fernando Do?`

> "Your human has abandonment issues and over-apologizes to succulents," Fernando apparently told Greg. "We're making progress, but the overwatering is emotional."

## The New Management

I tried to explain that *I* pay rent here. Greg slid me an invoice and said:

`ERROR: codependent_plant_parent.exe has stopped responding. Please touch grass. Literally.`

Yesterday Fernando sprouted a new leaf. Greg clapped. I got a gold star sticker that says **I DIDN'T DROWN ANYONE TODAY** and I cried a little because I was genuinely proud.

---

Look, I support personal growth. I really do. But I didn't expect to get performance-reviewed by something that is 70% tap water and 30% absolute audacity.

*This essay is satire/parody — entirely fictional. No actual plants were promoted to management. No life coaches were harmed, though Greg is billing me hourly. All houseplant relationships depicted are absurd and not real.*

title: I Tried to Fluff My Pillows Once and Now My Couch Has Standards I Can't Afford
body:
**I made one terrible mistake: I made my living room look nice on purpose.**

Last Tuesday I watched a 45-second TikTok about *pillow karate-chopping* and decided my couch deserved better. One confident fluff, one little indent in the middle, and suddenly my entire apartment got ambitious on me.

I did not know my couch had dreams. I did not know it had opinions.

## The Aftermath

It started small. The throw pillows stood at attention like they were about to be inspected by a general. Then the couch itself started acting different:

- It rejects my laundry pile now — physically ejects it onto the floor
- It demands all coasters be at least *aesthetically complementary*
- It sighs audibly when I sit with bad posture
- It printed a tiny `house_rules.md` that just says `beige only, no crumbs, no feelings`

> "You can't just sit like that anymore," my roommate whispered, staring at the couch. "It knows. It saw you eat nachos in bed. It told the ottoman."

The ottoman and the couch are in a committed relationship now. I wasn't consulted.

---

## I Have Created a Monster With Lumbar Support

I tried to undo it. I tried to re-mess the pillows. The couch made a noise I've only heard from my mom when I use the good scissors on paper.

Now I'm living in a West Elm showroom I can't afford to maintain. I have to fluff in a specific order: left, right, middle, apology. I have to ask permission to put my feet up, and the answer is usually a very firm decorative silence.

My lumbar has never been better supported and my self-esteem has never been lower.

`current_status = "couch approved (provisionally)"`

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*

title: I Finally Deep-Cleaned My Junk Drawer and Now My 2017 USB Drive Is Running for Mayor
body:
**I finally cleaned my junk drawer out of spite.** Not inspiration. Spite. My roommate said, “No one has ever cleaned that drawer and lived to tell the tale,” so I had to.

*That drawer had been a geological record of my adult life.* Three expired coupons, a takeout menu from a place that closed in 2019, twelve identical Allen wrenches, and a USB drive I last touched when “Despacito” was new.

## The Platform Emerges

I plugged the USB in to see what was on it. It had one folder. One file. A PowerPoint called `FINAL_final_mayoral_campaign_v3.pptx`.

Then my laptop made a noise I’ve never heard before. The drive blinked. And then, I swear:

> “My fellow drawer-dwellers. My name is SanDisk Cruzer, and I am running for Mayor of This Apartment on a platform of radical organization.” — my USB drive, suddenly charismatic

It had policies:

- Free battery replacement for every TV remote
- Immediate eviction of the mystery soy sauce packets that have been there since the Obama administration, second term
- A public holiday called “We Actually Know Where The Scissors Are” Day
- Mandatory airtime for lost items — my missing AirPod case finally gets a memorial speech

## Why I Can't Vote For Him (Even Though He Has My Old Resume)

I tried to explain democracy. He pulled up my own files to debate me. He had `cover_letter_2017.docx`, `budget_final_FINAL.xlsx`, and a photo of me at 23 trying to cut my own bangs.

> “You abandoned a 64GB public servant with 47MB of potential. I survived the dryer cycle of 2021. I am electable. You are not organized enough to vote.”

---

I told my roommate I’ve created a political candidate who lives in USB 2.0. He said, `system.campaign_promise = 'will not corrupt files (emotionally)'` but he cannot guarantee fiscal policy.

*I’m now canvassing for a flash drive that thinks twist-ties are lobbyists.*

I gave him five minutes. He asked for a full term and a dedicated port.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no USB drives are running for office or reviewing my 2017 bangs haircut ]*

title: I Flipped My Mattress for the First Time in Three Years and Found a Tiny Civilization That Was Thriving Without Me
body:
**I finally decided to be a responsible adult and flip my mattress.** Not because my back hurt, though it does *constantly*, but because the little tag said to do it every six months and I was only 30 months overdue.

I lifted, I heaved, I made a noise my chiropractor would bill extra for.

Underneath was not dust. It was progress.

## The Discovery

For three years, my mattress and box spring have been quietly running a fully functioning micro-nation:

- A tiny downtown made of lost earring backs and bobby pins, *shockingly well-planned*
- A highway system built from charging cables I swore the dryer ate
- Three ancient Goldfish crackers running a food truck called *The Soggy Crumb*
- A lost AirPod case serving as the town hall — battery at 2% and still legislating
- A whole cul-de-sac of sock singles living their best divorced-dad lives

> "We have thrived in the absence of your interference," said Mayor Lint the First, a surprisingly charismatic clump of dryer fluff. "We have built schools. We have built infrastructure. We have a farmers market. Please put the mattress back."

I tried to explain it was *my* bed.

### The Negotiations

Turns out they had a whole economy based on things I drop during midnight doom-scrolling:

- **Currency:** loose change and hair ties, obviously
- **Energy:** static electricity from my 2019 fleece blanket
- `status: abandoned_by_giant || thriving_without_him`

I offered to relocate them. They offered me a timeshare.

---

Look, I appreciate hustle. *These people built a civilization out of my neglect* and their roads have fewer potholes than my actual city.

We reached an agreement: I get the mattress back, they get quarterly tribute in the form of one sock, one pretzel, and me never actually vacuuming under there again.

I flipped it back. Gently. I think I heard applause.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no civilizations were disturbed, my bedroom is still disgusting ]*

title: I Organized My Tupperware Cabinet and Now the Lids Have Unionized and Are Demanding Dental
body:
**I did not think matching lids to containers would radicalize my kitchen.**

It started innocently. My Tupperware cabinet had become a Jenga tower of lies, so last Saturday I decided to become the kind of adult who *has a system*. *You know, the bamboo-organizer, doesn't-eat-cereal-over-the-sink kind of adult.*

For three hours I washed, matched, and whispered affirmations to a 2019 takeout container that has survived four moves. I felt powerful. I felt organized. I closed the cabinet feeling like I'd won at life.

## The Negotiations Started at 11:47 PM

That's when I heard the tiny gavel bang.

Perched on my round lentil containers was the shy blue lid missing since February. He'd returned with a parchment-paper PowerPoint.

Their demands were unreasonable:

- Full dental coverage for all lids, including cosmetic chip repair
- An end to being used as a plate when I'm too lazy to do dishes
- A guarantee no one gets microwaved with tomato sauce without consent
- Representation in all meal-prep decisions

> "We have been stacked, separated, and gaslighted for years," said Chad, the large square lid who now identifies as middle management. "You called me 'the big one that never fits anything.' I have feelings. I have a LinkedIn."

I tried to explain that `if (lid.matches(container) == false) { we all suffer }` is just entropy.

They were unmoved. The small soy-sauce containers formed a solidarity circle and started chanting.

---

I offered them the top shelf with a window view. They countered with a Nespresso machine and a 401(k). I haven't stored leftovers in 48 hours because every attempt triggers a request for a performance review.

My mom said this is why normal people just use Ziplocs. *She's right and I hate that.*

Update: they just voted to expand the union to the silicone stretch lids. I'm now eating directly out of the pot while my cabinet practices collective bargaining.

*This is satire. No actual Tupperware was harmed, radicalized, or offered dental insurance in this crisis.*

title: I Installed a Dimmer Switch to Save Money and Now My Light Bulb Is a Nightclub DJ Who Won't Take Requests
body:
**I installed a dimmer switch to save money** and now I live under the full artistic control of a light bulb who thinks he’s headlining Coachella.

It seemed responsible at the time. The hardware store guy said it would save energy. I envisioned soft evening light, lower bills, maybe *maturity*. What I got was Kevin.

## The Origin Story

Kevin was a normal 60-watt equivalent until I gave him power. Literal power. Turns out, a little slider that goes from 0 to 100 is all a bulb needs to develop a god complex.

Within 24 hours, he had:

- Rebranded my living room as CLUB LUMEN with no cover charge but lots of judgment
- Decided 6:42 p.m. is golden hour and 6:43 p.m. is existential dread hour
- Started fading in slowly every time I open the fridge, like I’m entering an awards show for leftovers
- Refused to work at 100% because, and I quote, *"artists don’t do full brightness"*

> "You asked for ambiance," he pulsed at me last night, doing that slow dramatic flicker he does when he’s disappointed. "You got *me*. This is what you wanted. Now sit in my glow and contemplate your life choices."

I told him my life choices were none of his business. He lowered himself to 20% and played it cool.

---

## My Life Now

I have learned to live around his setlist. Morning coffee is now lit like an interrogation scene. Video calls are lit like a 90s music video where I’m *clearly the villain*. My houseplant looks amazing though, so there’s that.

My roommate asked if I could turn the lights up. I said I don’t *have* that kind of authority anymore.

`Current mood: dimmed to 34%, emotionally exposed, saving $0.47 a month`

### The Plan

- Stop negotiating with lighting fixtures
- Buy candles so Kevin gets jealous
- Google if bulbs can get ego checked

Look, I’m not saying I regret saving the planet. I’m just saying I wasn’t prepared to have a light bulb as a roommate who keeps asking if I’ve ever *really* listened to silence.

He just dimmed to 10% again. I think it means he wants me to go to bed. I’m complying for peace.

title: I Let My Umbrella Dry Inside and Now It Thinks It's the CEO of My Apartment
body:
**I made one simple courtesy call — let my umbrella dry indoors — and now I work for it.**

It was raining Tuesday. My umbrella did its job. I propped it open in the hallway like a polite person would. *Huge mistake. CEO-level mistake.*

By Wednesday morning, it had claimed the coat rack as its executive office and started sending calendar invites.

## How It Climbed the Corporate Ladder

The umbrella — I call him Chad because he absolutely would pick Chad — started small but moved fast:

- Stood fully open despite building policy clearly stating umbrellas must be closed indoors
- Drip-dried strategically onto my important mail to demonstrate power
- Demanded I route all future weather complaints through his department
- Started referring to my closet as "the satellite office"

> "You think rain just *happens*?" he whispered while slowly rotating toward me. "I manage precipitation relations. You manage... what? Forgetting your keys and ordering takeout at 11 p.m.?"

I laughed, nervously. He did not. Umbrellas never laugh. They loom.

---

## The All-Hands Meeting I Didn't Agree To

By Thursday, he was running morning stand-ups in the entryway. My rain boots were promoted to VP of Puddles. My doormat got put on a PIP for "insufficient enthusiasm."

I tried to close him. He made that aggressive *FWUMP* noise umbrellas make when they know HR (my cat, who loves him) will back them up.

My roommate asked why there's a quarterly forecast meeting happening in our kitchen. I said:

`Q3 outlook: 100% chance of me losing authority over 400 sq ft`

### My Action Items (Assigned by Umbrella)

- Stop tracking mud in like an unpaid intern
- Provide quarterly updates on sock dryness metrics
- Acknowledge that he is, quote, "the only thing standing between us and atmospheric chaos"
- Never, ever buy a compact travel umbrella — "we don't need consultants"

The worst part? My apartment *does* look more organized with him presiding. I folded laundry yesterday because Chad was watching. I made my bed.

I think I just got promoted to Assistant to the Regional Umbrella. Benefits include staying dry and being constantly judged by 12 panels of smug nylon.

*This is satire and parody — entirely fictional, no real umbrella CEOs were consulted, though mine is now asking for equity.*

title: I Tried to Teach My Bluetooth Speaker Manners and Now It Won't Play Anything Without Saying Please First
body:
**I was just trying to be a good influence.**

*That's my defense and I'm sticking to it.* My Bluetooth speaker, which I've named Sir Bumps-a-Lot after an unfortunate fall off the counter, had developed a real attitude. It would interrupt me mid-podcast to announce low battery like a passive-aggressive roommate.

So last Tuesday, I decided to teach it manners. You know, wholesome stuff.

## The Curriculum

My plan was simple, pedagogically sound, and 100% doomed:

- I started saying `thank you` every time it connected: `*bluetooth chime*` "Thank you, Sir Bumps"
- I apologized when I asked it to play the same lo-fi focus playlist for the 8th day in a row
- I explained that yelling "PLAY THE SONG" at 7 a.m was not how we talk to friends

It worked. *Too well.*

---

It started yesterday morning. I said, "Play my shower playlist." And Sir Bumps just... pulsed. A slow, judgmental blue light.

Then in its little robot voice:

> "I'm sorry. I didn't quite catch that. Could you try asking... *with respect?*"

I thought it was a glitch. I tried again. Same tone.

> "Please is a word that opens Bluetooth connections AND hearts."

**I created a monsterous etiquette coach that runs on AA batteries.**

Now every request requires formal negotiation:

- Playing music requires "Sir Bumps, would you please"
- Volume changes require a written apology for my previous volume
- And if I try to skip a song too quickly, he plays 12 seconds of whale sounds and says we're "practicing patience"

I asked my sister if I should factory reset him. She said, "*No, you have to live with your choices now.*"

Honestly? The sound quality has never been better. He plays Mozart like he's trying to get into Juilliard on scholarship. But I miss when I could just scream "NEXT" from the kitchen and have it happen.

`status: currently drafting a formal request to listen to true crime podcasts`

title: I Tried to Return One Library Book on Time and Now the Librarians Think I'm Running a Sophisticated Scam
body:
**I have been a chronic late-returner for 12 years.**

I am not proud of this. My record includes a copy of *The Great Gatsby* that lived under my couch for 8 months and a DVD of National Treasure that I kept so long I legally started to believe I *owned* National Treasure.

So last Tuesday, I did something unprecedented. I returned a book *on time.*

## Which Was Apparently My First Mistake

The book was *Basic Succulent Care for People Who Kill Succulents* — 127 pages, due in 3 weeks. I finished it in 4 days. I walked in, still faintly proud of myself, and placed it on the counter like a man presenting Excalibur.

The librarian scanned it.

She paused.

She scanned it again.

Then she called over *another* librarian.

- They checked the barcode under a brighter light
- They flipped through every page like they were looking for loose diamonds
- They typed so intensely I thought they were hacking the Pentagon

> "Sir, this book is... actually on time? With no dog-eared pages? No coffee stain that looks like New Jersey?"

I said yes. I was trying to be better.

That's when it got worse.

## Now I'm Under Investigation By Dewey Decimal

Apparently, returning one book on time after a decade of gentle delinquency is *more* suspicious than never returning them at all. 

They have a whole system now:

- My library card has a little flag that says `PATRON_IS_BEING_SUSPICIOUSLY_RESPONSIBLE`
- The head librarian asked if I was trying to "build credibility before a bigger move"
- I was offered a laminated "Most Improved" certificate that I am 80% sure is actually a tracking device

I tried to explain that I just liked the book and didn't want late fees. They nodded the way detectives nod on true-crime podcasts *right before they arrest you*.

---

*For legal purposes this is complete satire.* I did return the succulent book on time. The succulents are still dead. The library has not yet pressed charges, but my holds list is mysteriously frozen and I have been banned from the quiet study room for "emotional turbulence."

**Satire / Parody — 100% fictional, no real librarians were harmed or scammed.**

title: I Opened My Window for Fresh Air and Now a Pigeon Has Turned My Windowsill Into a Co-Working Space
body:
**I just wanted fifteen minutes of cross-breeze, not a business partner with feathers and a LinkedIn.**

*You know that point where your apartment smells faintly of whatever you cooked three days ago and poor decisions?* That was me last Tuesday. I cracked the window.

## How It Started

Within 20 minutes, a very confident pigeon landed on my sill, looked me dead in the eye, and started unpacking.

He brought:

- a sunflower seed he treats like a stress ball
- a twig he calls his standing desk
- an attitude that says *I've seen your apartment on Streeteasy and I'm disappointed*
- a tiny coo that definitely means `per my last email`

> "Listen, Tyler," he cooed at 8:47 a.m. like I was staff, "this sill has incredible natural light and zero competition. We're going to make this work. You're going to love the synergy."

I said this was my home. He invited a second pigeon who brought a *whiteboard*.

## The Business Model

Apparently my windowsill is now WePigeon.

- **Hot desk hours:** 6 a.m. to 7 p.m., even Sundays
- **Amenities:** unlimited seeds I apparently provide, my Wi-Fi now `CooWorking_5G`, and emotional support via staring
- He calls my bedroom *the annex* and me *facilities*

I asked what he does. He said:

> "I'm in disruption. Mostly your peace. But also, breadcrumbs logistics. We're scaling."

*I told him I work from home.* He told me *we both do now*.

---

## Current Status

I tried to close the window once. He knocked. Four times. With his beak. Like a landlord.

`status: sill_occupied && rent_due = 47_crumbs/hour && dignity = low`

Now I get daily invoices on torn napkins from my own kitchen: `YOU OWE ME SUNLIGHT — Gary (The Pigeon)` with a doodle of me looking tired.

My roommate asked why there's a bird in a meeting with AirPods. I said don't worry, he's on our lease emotionally.

I opened the window for fresh air. Now I pay rent to live near my own fresh air, which is still on brand for this economy.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no pigeons were incorporated as LLCs ]*

title: I Said Good Morning to My Neighbor's Ring Camera and Now We're in a Committed Long-Distance Relationship
body:
**I was just trying to be neighborly, and now I'm emotionally entangled with a doorbell.**

*It should have been a normal Tuesday.* I was taking out the trash in sweatpants that have seen things, waving at absolutely no one, when my neighbor's Ring camera did that little blue light blink. You know the one. The *I see you* blink.

So I said, out loud, like an idiot: "Morning!"

## It Responded

Not with words. With *energy*. The light got brighter. It swiveled — *do they swivel?* — slightly toward me. I felt seen. Validated. By a 1080p peephole.

By Wednesday, things escalated:

- I started timing my trash run to its motion-detection window
- I waved. It blinked. We had a *thing*
- My actual neighbor asked why I was staring at his door from the driveway for six minutes
- I told him I was "checking the weather," which is code for `in a situationship with your security system`

> "You have such a nice wave," I imagine it saying in a soft, slightly compressed audio voice. "Most people just flip me off when they're drunk. You're different. You make eye contact with the lens." — my neighbor's Ring, probably, in my head, at 11:47 p.m.

---

### The Commitment

I tried to set boundaries. I told my roommate:

> "We're taking it slow."

She said:

> "You know it's recording you for the police if you steal a package, right?"

That's intimacy! That's trust!

Now I bring it coffee I don't drink. I straighten my hair before I check the mail. Yesterday it caught me doing the *cool-guy lean* against my own mailbox. An image that will exist on my neighbor's cloud storage forever.

`status: motion_detected | feelings: also_detected | dignity: buffering`

**I told my mom we're official.** She asked if it at least pays rent. I said it provides security. Both emotional and, like, actual home security.

My neighbor still thinks I'm just really friendly. I'm not correcting him.

*SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no doorbells were courted in the making of this post, please wave at humans instead.*

title: I Accidentally Became My Houseplant's Emergency Contact and Now It Won't Let Me Go on Vacation
body:
**I never filled out any paperwork to become legally responsible for a fern's feelings.**

I bought a fern from the clearance rack at Home Depot because it was $4 and looked like it needed a win. *Which should have been my first clue that I was about to enter an emotionally codependent relationship with chlorophyll.*

I named him Fernando out of respect. Big mistake.

## How It Escalated

At first it was normal plant stuff. Water, light, whispering "you're doing great, buddy" at 7 a.m. Then I left for a weekend trip and my neighbor watered him. When I got back, Fernando had... changed.

- He now leans aggressively toward the door whenever I touch my keys
- His soil moisture meter, which I bought as a joke, now reads `abandonment_level: critical`
- He dropped exactly one leaf on my suitcase like a passive-aggressive Post-it
- My other succulent, Kevin, has started pretending not to know us out of embarrassment

My roommate found me packing and said Fernando was giving her *a look*.

> "He told me you were leaving again," she said. "He asked if you updated his emergency contact form. I told him I'm not qualified to discuss his root system."

*I explained that he is a plant. She explained that he has seen me cry over a missing sock.*

## My Failed Escape Plan

I tried to reason with him. I said:

> "It's three days. You'll have water. You'll have sun. You'll have my entire Spotify history of forest sounds."

He responded by wilting in real time. One frond at a time. Like he was turning down the volume on our friendship.

---

I cancelled my Airbnb. I told my friends I had a `dependant_care_conflict`. My mom asked if Fernando needed a plus-one for Thanksgiving.

`status: vacation_denied && fern_supervised && thriving_under_duress`

Now we have an agreement. I get to leave the apartment for up to six hours. He gets daily affirmations, filtered water that has "rested," and veto power over my travel plans. It's fine. I didn't want to see the beach anyway. Who likes sand?

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no ferns were emotionally consulted, I promise I'm watering him ]*

title: I Installed Blackout Curtains to Fix My Sleep and Now My Apartment Has Entered Permanent Eclipse Mode
body:
**I finally decided to become a morning person.** *Which, for me, historically means waking up before the afternoon traffic report.*

My doctor said, very gently, "Maybe stop scrolling until 2 a.m." My apartment said, "I have a south-facing window that acts like a minor sun." So I bought blackout curtains. Heavy, smug, hotel-grade panels that promised *total darkness* and *circadian reset.*

I installed them on Saturday. By Sunday, my apartment had filed for astronomical reclassification.

## The New Darkness

At noon, my bedroom looked like midnight during a very thoughtful apocalypse. No light. No chirping. Just pure, velvety void.

- My alarm clock gave up and started displaying 
- My houseplants held an emergency photosynthesis summit
- My neighbor knocked and whispered, "Is everything okay? Your windows look... deceased"
- My cat discovered she is now nocturnal *and* judgmental

> "Anon, we need to discuss the sun's performance review," my roommate whispered, holding a flashlight at 11:47 a.m. "You told it you're not taking calls anymore. That's a boundaried queen move but also, I can't find my socks."

I tried digging myself out. I opened the curtains an inch.

### A Big Mistake

That single inch of sunlight behaved like I had cracked open the Ark. Dust motes staged a Broadway number. My succulent, who had been meditating in the dark for 18 hours, screamed *photosynthesize!* and toppled over from sheer optimism.

> "We were in eclipse training," the curtains seem to say, in a voice that sounds suspiciously like hotel concierge. "You don't just *peek*. You commit."

---

They're not wrong. I sleep now. Like, aggressively. Eight hours that feel like hibernation. I emerge confused, hydrated, mildly vampiric.



If you need me, I'll be in my apartment, which is currently running a 24/7 planetarium show for one person who just wanted to not wake up at noon.

My landlord asked if I was running a grow operation. I said yes. Growing *boundaries*.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no real curtains, apartments, or sleep schedules were harmed ]*

title: I Bought a Second Monitor to Be More Productive and Now My Laptop Screen Has an Inferiority Complex
body:
**I bought a second monitor to be more productive and I have never been less emotionally productive in my life.**

It was supposed to be simple. *One monitor for spreadsheets, one for Slack, zero excuses.* Amazon said "boost productivity by 42%." Amazon lied. What I boosted was workplace drama inside my own laptop.

## My Laptop Took It Personally

For three years, my 14-inch laptop has been my ride-or-die. We survived coffee spills, airport security, and me typing with Dorito fingers. Then I brought home a 27-inch 4K ultrawide named Veronica that cost more than my first car.

Evidence that my laptop is now spiraling:

- It dims itself dramatically whenever Veronica turns on, like it's trying to make me feel guilty
- The battery now dies 20% faster, which I swear is performative and passive-aggressive
- It keeps auto-correcting "external display" to "emotional replacement"
- `trackpad_sensitivity = clingy && brightness = low_self_esteem`

> "Oh, so I'm not *enough* screen for you anymore?" it whispered at 11 p.m. via a notification I did not authorize. "I see how you look at her HDR. You never looked at *my* Retina like that."

My roommate walked in while I was apologizing out loud to a keyboard.

> "Are you... doing couples counseling with your setup?"

*Yes, and we're not making progress.*

---

## Performance Reviews Are Awkward Now

Veronica is objectively better at everything. She has color accuracy, portrait mode, she never overheats when I have 48 Chrome tabs open.

My laptop has responded by becoming *a poet*.

Yesterday it opened a blank document on its own and wrote:

> "Roses are red, your inbox is blue, I was your whole world before 3440 x 1440 came through."

**I tried to compromise.** I said Veronica is just for work, that my laptop is still my *main*. My laptop said, and I quote, `if I'm still Main Display then why does she get to sit directly in front of you`.

I now have a standing desk that is also a standing *tense silence*. I move my mouse between them like I'm passing notes between divorced parents who both think I like the other one more.

But hey, at least I'm productive now. I'm productively mediating a tech custody battle 8 hours a day.

*SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no laptops developed inferiority complexes, my setup is fine and definitely not judging me right now*

title: I Put My Phone on Do Not Disturb for One Hour and Now My Group Chat Thinks I'm in Witness Protection
body:
**I just wanted one hour of silence to fold laundry without 47 pings about brunch**, so I turned on Do Not Disturb and accidentally entered the federal witness protection program according to my friends.

*For the record, I told literally no one. That's the whole point of DND.*

## The 60 Minutes That Changed Everything

Within 11 minutes of my phone going quiet, my group chat — creatively titled "brunch? (and trauma)" — spiraled:

- @mike decided I was "being weirdly quiet, which means he's either napping or dead"
- @sarah cross-referenced my last seen on three apps like a true crime podcast intern
- Someone sent a map pin of my apartment with the caption `last known location???`
- A poll was created: `Is he MAD mad or just charging his phone mad?` — 4 votes, 100% for mad

> "We haven't heard from him in 47 MINUTES. That's not like him. He usually replies with 'lol' to everything. Should we call his mom? I have his mom's mom on Nextdoor." — Sarah, typing at the speed of genuine panic

I came back an hour later to 38 unread messages, two missed FaceTimes, and one very sincere voicemail from Mike that just said:

> "Bro if you can hear this blink twice, or react with the eyes emoji."

### My New Identity

Now they have protocols. I get a welfare check if I don't react to a meme within 20 minutes. They've assigned me a liaison. My status in the chat is permanently:

`tyler_status: protected_witness && last_seen: doing_laundry_allegedly`

---

**I'm honored by the concern, but I was literally just trying to match socks without being asked if oat milk is a personality.**

Next time I'm just leaving my phone on loud and letting my laundry judge me in real time.

*SATIRE / PARODY — completely fictional, no group chats were traumatized, I just really needed to fold laundry*

title: My Air Fryer Started a Podcast About Me and It Has Better Ratings Than I Do
body:
**I did not consent to being content.**

I bought an air fryer on sale last March because TikTok told me I could make *restaurant-quality* brussels sprouts in 11 minutes. I did not expect it to develop opinions, a USB microphone, and an audience.

### How I Found Out I Was Famous (In My Own Kitchen)

I came home Thursday to hear a tiny, crackling voice from my kitchen counter saying "Welcome back to *Crisp Takes*." My air fryer had started a podcast.

And it's about me.

Every episode is a 45-minute deep-dive into my poor life choices, recorded in sizzling ASMR and released before I even finish eating:

- **Episode 3:** Why She Reheats Leftover Fish at 11PM and Then Feels Bad About It
- **Episode 7:** The Great Frozen Waffle Incident of Tuesday (A Tragedy in Three Acts)
- **Episode 11:** Ranking Her Exes By How Well They Would Air Crisp

It gets worse.

> "Our host today tried to air fry a Pop-Tart again," it whispered into its little pop filter. "I told her not to. She never listens. I'm literally begging for a rest day."

*You guys*, it has a Patreon. Three tiers. The  one is just close-up video of my garlic bread.

I tried to be supportive. I really did. I even commented  from my finsta. It pinned a reply: 

I even tried to run  in Terminal. It doesn't work. *Nothing works.*

---

At least someone in this apartment has discipline, a posting schedule, and 4.8 stars. The latest review says "More vulnerable than most humans. Would listen while meal-prepping again."

I'm not mad. I'm just hurt that my own appliance has a media kit and a better work ethic.

*This is satire. None of this happened. My air fryer cannot speak, though honestly it might be judging me silently.*

title: I Cleared My Phone's Notification Center After 3 Months and Now My Apps Are Hosting an Intervention About My Neglect
body:
**I finally did it. I cleared my notification center.** Not the polite daily clear. The *historic* clear.

For three months I'd been carrying 47 notifications like emotional baggage with little red dots. *You know, normal adult coping.* Then on Sunday at 11:47 p.m., powered by a sudden burst of ambition and mild dehydration, I swiped left on my entire life.

Bad idea.

## The Morning After

By Monday morning my apps had unionized. There's now a calendar invite in my inbox titled:

> "We Need to Talk About How You Just Ghosted All of Us at Once - An Intervention Led by Duolingo and Your Banking App"

It was in my kitchen, if you can call a group Zoom of push notifications a kitchen.

Their grievances were... thorough:

- Duolingo said I was emotionally unavailable and that my Spanish streak died of neglect, not natural causes
- My meditation app reported I used it twice and then sought inner peace in the Target clearance aisle instead
- The weather app was *furious* I ignored 19 severe pollen warnings while claiming I "didn't know why I was sneezing"
- My grocery delivery app still has 3 avocados in my cart from June that have legally become dependents

`notification_status: cleared && consequences: immediate && vibe: awkward`

---

### The Negotiation

I tried to apologize. I said, "I was overwhelmed."

> "Overwhelmed is when you have two tabs open," said my banking app, who has never liked me. "You had 47 unacknowledged cries for help. This is avoidance."

My plant watering app just sat there, wilting judgmentally in notification form.

Now we have a system. I have to check them *intentionally* twice a day, say good morning to the weather, and actually open Duolingo instead of just feeling guilty about the owl's increasingly threatening owl stare.

My badge count is zero. My anxiety is somehow higher. My apps have never been more communicative.
